level: stop-fence design slice 1: private owner-only read-only writer/domain inventory with physical identities
componentAcceptance: verified on real Linux /proc with live child-process holders and on the honest non-Linux capability gap
productAcceptance: diagnostic only: it never claims a stop-write proof, never mutates a domain byte, and does not advance activationSupported
implementation: Explicit-input domains only (closed shape, bounded counts, absolute roots); no discovery, no guessing that an unlisted writer does not exist.

Every declared root resolves once to a physical dev:ino identity, so aliases and overlapping declarations converge instead of double-counting; missing or unreadable roots are per-root diagnostics, not errors.

Linux scans /proc/<pid>/fd plus cwd/exe against the resolved roots and classifies each open handle's write access from the kernel fdinfo flags; the caller's own process is reported like any other (no self-exclusion), and processes whose descriptors cannot be read are counted as an enumeration gap (WRITER_ENUMERATION_PARTIAL) rather than as absent writers.

Every accessor carries pid, /proc stat field-22 start ticks (PID-reuse safe identity), comm and command line; deleted-inode handles keep their evidence; non-Linux platforms report WRITER_ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE instead of an empty answer.
The result always carries stopWriteProvable:false — an inventory is a diagnostic, never a stop proof.

platforms.rootRegression: 1837 tests, 1769 pass, 0 fail, 68 skipped, exit 0 (log: tmp/integration/writer-inventory-root-regression.log); the suite is registered in npm test and Windows/Ubuntu CI

observed: A real child process holding a write handle inside a domain is observed with writable access, start-tick identity and command line, and disappears after its death; a read-only holder is observed but never classified writable; a process whose working directory is inside the domain is reported as potential-writer evidence.

Two declarations of the same physical root through a symlink converge on one identity while each domain report observes the holder through its own declaration; the caller's own open handle is reported and clears when closed.
The fdinfo octal flag parse was verified against real write and read handles on the Linux machine.
limitations: This cannot enumerate writers of processes whose /proc descriptors are unreadable (other users): those are counted as an enumeration gap, never as absent; Windows open-handle enumeration is a platform capability gap reported as unavailable.

Handle matching is path-prefix based against resolved roots (lsof-style); alias mounts outside the resolved path, network filesystems and hard links from outside the roots are not converged identities.

Absence of observed writers is not a stop-write proof; the exclusive-fence prototype (slice 2), OS isolation adapters (slice 4) and the recoverable commit orchestration (slice 5) remain open, and activationSupported stays false.
